## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The rule is widely preserved across the monastic codes of early Buddhist schools. Within the Pali canon, it corresponds to rule 10 of the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha, rule 10 of the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha, and the respective Sekhiya sections of the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra. Parallels in other Vinaya lineages are preserved in Chinese and Sanskrit across the Dharmaguptaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, and Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda traditions, as well as the Chinese *Upāliparipṛcchā*. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 104 internal Pali matches across 50 texts, reflecting heavy formulaic sharing with other Sekhiya rules in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga, including Sekhiyas 16, 20, 11, 48, 7, and 24 [DharmaNexus]. None of the queried secondary literature passages relate to this text, as all instances of "SK 10" refer to verse 10 of the *Sāṃkhyakārikā* or other non-Vinaya works.

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
